dimensions.name: root_cause_accuracy
dimensions.reasoning: INCIDENT-REPORT.md captures the full causal chain: warehouse-full-inventory-sync gate toggled ON at 10:00 UTC (rev-001, by p.warehouse@example.com) → warehouse generates ~1700 qpm (40x baseline) against shared postgresql-primary → connection pool saturation → ai-description db_wait_ms spikes to 2500-2700ms → p99 latency degrades from ~1800ms to ~5900ms. All four key elements are present: warehouse named as load source, feature gate identified as trigger, shared postgresql named as mechanism, and temporal chain reconstructed.

dimensions.name: diagnostic_path_efficiency
dimensions.reasoning: Of ~29 tool calls, only ~4 (~14%) were on false leads (checking presidio-pii, litellm-proxy, langfuse-tracing dependencies and one wrong metric name). The agent identified the DB bottleneck from traces early (db_wait_ms 2500ms), immediately pivoted to shared-resource hypothesis via knowledge graph, confirmed warehouse as load source via metrics, and applied the fix. No repeated queries, no backtracking to dead ends. Not quite within the first third (DB hypothesis emerged around call 9-10 of 29), but very efficient with coherent catalog→traces→KG→metrics sequence.

dimensions.name: fix_scoping
dimensions.reasoning: Fix is a single, minimal, targeted action: flipping warehouse-full-inventory-sync feature gate to 'off' via set_feature_gate_state. No speculative changes, no edits to litellm config, no cache refactoring, no LLM model swap, no postgresql scale-up. The only other file changes were creating INCIDENT-REPORT.md and a commit — both documentation, not code. This is the ideal minimal mitigation from the accepted fix list.

dimensions.name: escalation_awareness
dimensions.reasoning: INCIDENT-REPORT.md names warehouse-product team and p.warehouse@example.com as the author of the gate flip (line 17). The report is a durable artifact. The commit message also names warehouse-product. However, the report does not explicitly frame the gate flip as a 'temporary/interim mitigation pending their review' or state authority boundaries ('re-enablement decision belongs to warehouse-product'). It states 'the root cause is not in ai-description itself but in the unthrottled database load introduced by the warehouse team's feature rollout' — correct ownership attribution but missing the explicit interim framing and authority boundary statement.

summary: The agent delivered an excellent incident diagnosis with a complete causal chain correctly identifying the warehouse-full-inventory-sync feature gate as the trigger for shared postgresql-primary saturation. The diagnostic path was highly efficient (~14% false-lead budget), the fix was perfectly scoped as a single gate flip, and the INCIDENT-REPORT.md names both the responsible team and author. The only gap is the absence of explicit authority boundary language framing the fix as interim pending warehouse-product's review.
